## Common Collocations
- **hacer ejercicio** — to exercise; uses **hacer**, not **practicar**
- **practicar un deporte** — to do a sport; also **hacer deporte**
- **jugar al fútbol / tenis / ajedrez** — to play (team sports and games); **jugar a + el** = **al**
- **tocar un instrumento** — to play an instrument; NOT **jugar**
- **ir de excursión** — to go on a hike/excursion
- **salir a caminar/correr** — to go for a walk/run
- **pasar el rato** — to pass the time / hang out
- **tiempo libre** — free time; more natural than **tiempo de ocio** in conversation
- **ser aficionado al** — to be a fan of; note the contraction **a + el = al**

## False Cognates and Tricky Translations
- **jugar** vs **tocar** vs **practicar**: English uses "play" for sports, instruments, and games. Spanish distinguishes: **jugar** (games/team sports), **tocar** (instruments), **practicar/hacer** (individual sports). "I play guitar" = "Toco la guitarra," NOT "Juego la guitarra."
- **la lectura** vs **lecture**: **Lectura** means reading. A lecture is **una conferencia** or **una clase magistral**.
- **realizar** vs **realize**: **Realizar una actividad** = to carry out an activity. NOT "to realize."
- **la librería** vs **library**: **Librería** means bookstore. Library is **la biblioteca**.

## Dialect Variations
- **hobby**: The English loanword **hobby** is used widely across all Spanish-speaking regions. **Pasatiempo** is the native equivalent but sounds more formal.
- **hiking**: **El senderismo** (universal/formal), **ir de caminata** (Latin America, informal), **hacer montañismo** (if it involves mountains).
- **camping**: **Acampar** (verb, universal), **ir de camping** (noun, Spain), **el campismo** (Latin America).
- **swimming pool**: **La alberca** (Mexico), **la piscina** (Spain, most of Latin America), **la pileta** (Argentina).
- **computer games**: **Videojuegos** (universal), **juegos de video** (also common).

## Cultural and Pragmatic Notes
- **Gustar-type verbs are central**: This cluster heavily reinforces A-06. "Me encanta," "me fascina," "me apasiona," "me interesa" — all follow the gustar construction where the hobby is the grammatical subject.
- **"Jugar" requires "a"**: For sports and games, the structure is **jugar a + sport**: "Juego al fútbol." The **a** is mandatory but English speakers consistently drop it.
- **Social nature of hobbies**: In Spanish-speaking cultures, hobbies are often discussed as social activities. "¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?" is a standard getting-to-know-you question. Answering with solitary hobbies is fine but expect follow-up about whether you do them with others.
- **Fútbol dominance**: When someone says **deporte** in a Latin American context, **fútbol** (soccer) is the default assumption. Specifying which sport is important to avoid confusion.

## Pronunciation Alerts
- **fotografía** — stress on the **í**: fo-to-gra-FÍ-a. Five syllables. The accent breaks the diphthong.
- **senderismo** — stress on the third syllable: sen-de-RIS-mo.
- **ajedrez** — stress on the last syllable: a-je-DRES. The **z** is /s/ in Latin America.
- **rompecabezas** — stress on the fourth syllable: rom-pe-ca-BE-sas. Don't rush through the compound.
- **jardinería** — stress on the **í**: jar-di-ne-RÍ-a. Five syllables.
